Hi Sofia + Acme platform team,

Thanks again for your time this morning — really appreciate the thoughtful questions about structured output and reliability. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned: 

What we heard
- Primary goal: replace brittle rule-based extraction with a function-calling flow that returns strict JSON matching your schema, with automatic retries and an E2E monitoring signal for "schema compliance rate."
- Non-goal for the eval: full canonical integration into production. We want a runbook and objective metrics to decide next steps (Dedicated capacity vs hosted).

Recommended models for the eval (initial):
- rw-infer-small-v2: lower latency, good for 1–3 field outputs during fast iteration.
- rw-infer-1.0-large-qual: higher-quality deterministic outputs for complex nested schemas and enumerations.
- quantized rw-infer-fast-q4: cost-optimized option if throughput looks important.

Artifacts I attached:
- redwood-eval-plan.pdf (end-to-end plan + acceptance criteria)
- acme-json-schema-sample.json (your schema from the call)
- eval-prompt-set.txt (3 canonical prompts + negative cases)
- runbook-eval-checklist.md (what we measure, logging hooks)

Immediate asks / next steps
1) Confirm a 2-week eval window (we suggested Mar 9–20).
2) Approve the acceptance criteria in the plan (schema compliance >= 98% for required fields; retry success >= 90% on first retry).
3) Can we loop in a technical lead for the run (we recommend Jordan Blake from our Solutions team and Ethan Park from product for any runtime config tuning)?

I'll spin up a dedicated eval workspace, wire the prompt set, and produce an initial bench doc with per-model schema compliance numbers. Attaching a Drive link to benchmarks and the HubSpot deal here: https://drive.google.com/drive/fake-benchmark-link and https://hubspot.com/deal/RDW-2026-ACME-17

Marissa, thanks — this is great and aligns with where we want to go. A few clarifications from our side before we kick off the formal window: 

Critical requirements
- Strict JSON schema compliance for the "order_event" payload. Fields are validated downstream; malformed JSON causes a 1–2 hour manual rollback. We need to measure both syntactic compliance and semantic adherence (enums, types).
- Retries must be idempotent. If the model returns a malformed payload, the retry should return a corrected payload without creating duplicate downstream side effects.
- We need an automated classification for "repairable" vs "unrepairable" outputs so we can route to human review.

Acceptance thresholds we want to see to move forward
- Schema compliance (required fields only) >= 98%
- Retry success rate (first retry) >= 90%
- Mean latency for validated JSON <= 450ms (95th percentile)

Can you have Jordan and Ethan propose a technical approach for:
1) How the function-calling path ensures strict JSON (e.g., function signature enforcement + post-parse validator).
2) Retry logic + idempotency guarantees (we run a token-level replay or a deterministic prompt wrapper).
3) Telemetry hooks we can validate (trace ids, per-call schema pass/fail, repair attempts).

We prefer Mar 9 start but flexible. Also please add a security contact for the SOC2 checklist later in the thread.

Thanks,
Sofia Ramos

Thanks for the context — listing a pragmatic plan and a few technical notes below. I can own the eval automation and reporting.

Quick plan
1) Sampling: target 2,000 calls per model across the three prompt families (happy path, partial data, adversarial). That gives ~6k total calls; should be enough to estimate compliance at the percent level.
2) Function-calling enforcement: use the runtime function signature feature + a strict schema validator (jsonschema v4) in the post-processor. Any parse failure goes to a deterministic repair pass (see below).
3) Retry strategy: three-stage approach
  - Stage A: deterministic re-call with system prompt instructing "output only JSON matching schema" and temperature=0.0.
  - Stage B: if Stage A fails, run a constrained repair prompt that extracts parseable key/value pairs and recompose JSON (this is best-effort).
  - Stage C: if still failing, flag for human review and mark as "unrepairable."
4) Idempotency: we will include a per-request idempotency token and a lightweight dedupe layer on the consumer side (server-side dedupe). Retries will be tagged and any downstream side effects gated behind a confirm step until JSON validated.
5) Metrics / telemetry: per-call trace_id, model_variant, prompt_id, schema_pass (true/false), repair_attempts (0/1/2), latency_ms. We'll surface these in the eval dashboard and provide raw CSV.

Example function call / validator snippet (pseudo):
----
Function signature: submit_order_event(order_event: JSON) -> status
Post-processor: if !jsonschema.validate(order_event, acme_schema): run deterministic_repair(order_event_raw)
----

I'll create a Jira ticket (JIRA-ACME-1214) for the automation and a short runbook. Proposed kickoff: Tue Mar 3 10:00am PT for 30 minutes to align on sampling and telemetry. If Acme prefers Mar 9 start, we can use this week to provision.

Attachments: runbook-eval-checklist.md, eval-prompt-set.txt

— Jordan Blake
